subtopics.title: Set and interval notation
subtopics.exposition: In set notation, {x : x ∈ R, x > 0} is read as the set of all x-values such that x is an element of the set of real numbers and is greater than 0. In set notation, {y : y ∈ N, 3 < y ≤ 5} is read as the set of all y-values such that y is a natural number, is greater than 3 and is less than or equal to 5. In set notation, {z : z ∈ Z, z ≤ 100} is read as the set of all z-values such that z is an integer and is less than or equal to 100. In interval notation the two endpoints are written inside brackets and separated by a semicolon, for example (3, 11). In interval notation, a round bracket indicates that the number is not included in the interval. In interval notation, a square bracket indicates that the number is included in the interval. In interval notation, round brackets are always used for positive and negative infinity. The interval (3, 11) includes all real numbers greater than but not equal to 3 and less than but not equal to 11. The interval (-∞, -2) includes all real numbers less than, but not equal to, -2. The interval [1, 9) includes all real numbers greater than or equal to 1 and less than but not equal to 9.

subtopics.title: Evaluate with function notation
subtopics.exposition: A function is a mathematical relationship between two variables, where every input variable has one output variable. In functions, the x-variable is known as the input or independent variable, because its value can be chosen freely. The calculated y-variable is known as the output or dependent variable, because its value depends on the chosen input value. Functions can take input from many variables, but always give the same output, unique to that function. For f(x) = 2x + 1, f(-3) = -5 means that when x = -3 the value of the function is -5. For f(x) = 2x + 1, x = 13 means that when x = 13 the value of the function is 27. To determine the output value for a given input, such as f(-3) for f(x) = 2x + 1, replace x with the input value (here -3) and calculate. To determine the input value that gives a given output, write the equation f(x) = output (here 2x + 1 = 27) and solve for x, which gives x = 13. Function notation is another way of writing a function: y = 2x + 1 can be written as f(x) = 2x + 1. f(x) = 2x + 1 is said as 'f of x is equal to 2x + 1'. Any letter can be used to name a function in function notation, for example g(x), h(x) or p(x). 'Find the value of the function for x = -3' can be written as 'find f(-3)'. 'Find the value of x that will give a y-value of 27' can be written as 'find x if f(x) = 27'. A function can be represented in words, for example: the relationship between two variables is such that one is always 5 less than the other. A function can be represented as an algebraic formula, for example f(x) = x - 5. A function can be represented by a mapping diagram.

subtopics.title: Represent functions as tables and graphs
subtopics.exposition: Functions can be expressed in many different ways for different purposes. A table of values lists the input variable (x) values in one row and the matching output variable (y) values in another, for example x = -3, 0, 5 with y = -8, -5, 0. A function can be represented as a set of ordered number pairs, for example (-3, -8), (0, -5), (5, 0). A function can be represented as a graph.

subtopics.title: Domain and range from graphs
subtopics.exposition: The domain of a function is the set of all independent x-values from which the function produces a single y-value for each x-value. The range is the set of all dependent y-values which can be obtained using an independent x-value. Graphs allow relationships to be visualised and are much easier to read and interpret than lists of numbers. When the graphs of two people's locations as functions of time are plotted, the place where the lines cross means that the two people meet each other at that time.
